 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Jared McCain, Alex Caruso, Aday Mara and Isaiah Hartenstein will start Wednesday’s game against the Trail Blazers. 
 The Thunder have made two changes to the lineup that started Tuesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers. With Ajay Mitchell out, Caruso moves into the starting lineup. The other change is Mara, who replaces Kenrich Williams. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Ajay Mitchell 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #25

 Ajay Mitchell (ankle) has been ruled out against the Trail Blazers on Wednesday. 
 Mitchell will be sidelined for the second night of OKC’s back-to-back, which will open up a spot in the starting unit. Alex Caruso, Micah Peavy and Nique Clifford are all candidates to take on more minutes, with one of them likely to start. 
 Alex Caruso 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #9 
 Alex Caruso (ankle) is not on the injury report for Wednesday’s game against the Cavaliers. 
 Caruso is back after missing Oklahoma City’s last three games with a sprained ankle. He’ll give the Thunder much-needed wing depth, with two-way contract rookie Josh Dix possibly falling out of the rotation. 
 Alex Caruso 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #9 
 Alex Caruso (ankle) is not expected to be out long term 
 After missing this third straight contest on Monday vs. the Cavs, Caruso is expected to not be out long term as his ankle sprain is not deemed serious. Even when the veteran guard gets back into the fold, the Thunder will still rely on the younger guys for heavy minutes. 
 Alex Caruso 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #9 
 Alex Caruso (ankle) is out for Monday’s game against the Cavaliers. 
 Monday’s game will be the third that Caruso has missed since spraining his right ankle during Oklahoma City’s October 26 win over the Suns. Injuries have forced the Thunder to go deep into their bench, with rookie Bennett Stirtz playing 25 minutes or more in each of the last three games. 
 Alex Caruso 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #9 
 Alex Caruso (ankle) is out for Saturday’s game against the Rockets. 
 Caruso will miss a second consecutive game with a sprained right ankle. The Thunder signed Ochai Agbaji on Friday to add wing depth, and he may play rotation minutes immediately. 
 Ochai Agbaji 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #30 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that Ochai Agbaji has been signed to the Thunder’s final roster spot. 
 Agbaji will fill out Oklahoma City’s depth, and with Jalen Williams (leg), Alex Caruso (ankle) and Cason Wallace (shoulder) all out, Agbaji could see some rotation minutes immediately. He’s only worth an add in deep leagues. 
 Alex Caruso 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #9 
 Alex Caruso (ankle) is out for Wednesday’s game against the Mavericks. 
 Caruso sprained his right ankle during Monday’s win over the Suns and did not return. Oklahoma City’s depth has taken significant hits over the last 48 hours, and Caruso’s absence likely means that two-way contract rookie Josh Dix will once again play rotation minutes. He played 22 minutes on Monday and went scoreless. 
 Alex Caruso 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #9 
 Alex Caruso (ankle) will not return Monday vs. Suns. 
 Caruso went to the locker room with an apparent ankle injury after Dillon Brooks accidentally fell on him. The Thunder are already dealing with injuries in the guard position, so it’s worth monitoring over the next few days. 
 Alex Caruso 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #9 
 Alex Caruso amassed 12 points (4-of-6 FGs, 0-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, two assists, one block and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s exhibition against the Bucks. 
 With Chet Holmgren and Isaiah Hartenstein sitting, Caruso made his first appearance of the preseason as a starter. The veteran wing shot well, hitting four of his six three-point attempts in 17 minutes. While Caruso has been a solid member of the Thunder rotation the last two seasons, injuries limited his fantasy impact. With the team trading Luguentz Dort, Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins during the offseason, Caruso’s role takes on added importance, potentially pushing him back into fantasy relevance. 
 Ajay Mitchell 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #25 
 Ajay Mitchell (calf) is out for Saturday’s Game 7 against the Spurs. 
 Saturday’s series finale will be the fourth consecutive game that Mitchell has missed since straining his right calf during Game 3 of the Western Conference Finals. Jalen Williams (hamstring) is also out for Game 7, which means the Thunder will once again lean heavily on Jared McCain. Alex Caruso and Isaiah Joe also have added importance due to the absences.

 Zach Edey scored two points (1-of-4 FGs), five rebounds, and a block in 19 minutes on Wednesday. 
 Largely, Edey has been disappointing this year. His numbers are down from his rookie year and the minutes are a career low. His FG% is down 11.4% from last season. His value with size is important to this team, but the Grizzlies have good backup centers with Isaiah Stewart and Quinten Post who can take minutes from him. It’s getting harder to hold in redraft leagues with the ups and downs.

 Jerome has had 5 straight games of at least 20 points which is awesome for fantasy owners. He led the team with a +9 in a five point loss.  Kel’el Ware produced eight points (3-of-8 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), five rebounds, one assist, one steal and three blocks in Wednesday’s loss to the Lakers.
 Myles Turner (rest) was given the night off, opening the door for Ware to make his first start of the season. The good news is that the 7-footer blocked three shots. The bad news is that he didn’t do much else in what was an underwhelming performance. Ware played 23 minutes, while Jericho Sims (four rebounds, one assist and one block), who has been out of the rotation on most nights, played 18 minutes. The question now is whether Ware is worth the risk of buying low.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Tyler Herro (knee) accounted for 27 points (8-of-16 FGs, 9-of-10 FTs), two rebounds, seven assists, one block and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Lakers.
 Herro’s knee injury, sustained during Sunday’s loss to the Celtics, sidelined him for just one game. With Herro logging 35 minutes and putting up strong numbers, this was an encouraging performance from the Bucks guard. Based on his ADP, fantasy managers expected Herro to provide middle-round value in nine-cat formats, and he’s lived up to those expectations so far. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Jaylen Wells scored 22 points (6-of-13 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), two rebounds, an assist, and five 3-pointers in loss to the Nuggets on Wednesday. 
 Jaylen’s shot making is what kept Memphis in this game with his 3PT shooting. His game is pretty empty apart from the 3’s and the points, but he’s still a very valuable player as a threat as a shooter. His value as an NBA player is very stable with how the NBA wants these wings shooters that can play good defense.

 Jaime Jaquez 
 MIL 
 Guard

 Player Stats

 Jaime Jaquez Jr. tallied 25 points (7-of-16 FGs, 9-of-9 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, two steals and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Lakers.
 After starting each of Milwaukee’s first 11 games, Jaquez was moved to the bench on Wednesday. Given his productivity, that may be a role the Bucks ask Jaquez to take on moving forward. Recording his first 20-point game since October 24 against the 76ers, Jaquez finished with a season-high 25 as part of a solid overall stat line. He was runner-up for NBA Sixth Man of the Year last season, so this isn’t a foreign role for Jaquez. And it may raise his fantasy ceiling if the Bucks continue to bring him off the bench. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Collin Sexton (head) finished Wednesday’s win over the Bucks with 10 points (4-of-8 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), one rebound, three assists and one steal.
 With Quentin Grimes (finger) unavailable for Wednesday’s game, Sexton’s role had added importance. Unfortunately, while he did hit double figures, the Lakers guard had to leave with just under seven minutes left in the fourth quarter. Sexton banged heads with Bucks guard Ryan Rollins, and both left the game and did not return. Sexton’s cut required sutures, but there were no reports that he might have to enter the league’s concussion protocol. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Walker Kessler amassed 10 points (5-of-10 FGs), 11 rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block in Wednesday’s win over the Bucks.
 The Lakers have played seven games in November, and Kessler has recorded a double-double in six of them. In addition to the double-doubles, the 7-footer has blocked at least one shot in 11 of 13 games this season. Thus far, Kessler has been everything that fantasy managers hoped he would be in Los Angeles, and then some.

 Sandro Mamukelashvili accounted for 23 points (9-of-15 FGs), three rebounds, two assists, one steal and five three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Bucks.
 Mamukelashvili was at his best during the second quarter, shooting 4-of-4 from the field and scoring 10 points. He didn’t provide much beyond points and three-pointers, but Mamu has been productive enough this season to merit a roster spot in deep leagues. Despite not playing the same position, Mamukelashvili would be worth streaming if either Luka Dončić (ankle) or Austin Reaves (heel) misses Friday’s game against the Spurs. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson
